title: Reading the bill: SKU, sustained use and committed use discounts

videos.script: A machine is not one line on the bill. It is four or five. {{lines}} Its processors are one SKU, its memory another, its disk a third, its traffic a fourth. Each has a unit and a price, and each carries the region. {{region}} So the machine type is not on the bill at all. To ask what one machine cost, you filter by its labels. {{labels}} Then come the discounts. The first one nobody asks for. A machine that runs most of the month is billed less for each hour past the first quarter. {{sud}} You will work out the tiers yourself, with a short program and an example price: nothing for a quarter of the month, thirty percent for all of it. {{program}} The second discount is a contract. Promise a year or three of use, and pay less for it, whether the use happens or not. {{cud}} The two never add up. Google applies one, and only then the next, to whatever is left. {{order}} And when a bill arrives wrong, the cure is always the same. Find the SKU, find the project, read the labels. {{end}}
